An iron worker died and one other was injured after scaffolding collapsed in Chicago. Officials say two men were working on the University of Chicago cancer pavilion when high winds caused the scaffolding to collapse leaving the two to fall eight stories. One of the men had died on site while the other was transported to a hospital in critical condition, but survived. Winds during the day were regularly gusting between 40 and 45 mph around the city with a peak wind gust of 51 mph measured at Midway Airport that afternoon.

On the morning of the 17th, two 16-year-olds, one boy and one girl, were on a raft near Montrose Beach when strong winds allegedly caused their raft to flip over. A bystander pulled the girl to shore but officials were unable to recover the boy before he drowned. At the time, winds at Montrose harbor were peaking in the 20-23 kt range and the Chicago pier buoy was recording wave heights of 1 to 1.5 ft.

Four people required rescuing while swimming near Lighthouse Beach during the afternoon of the 30th. Three of the four swimmers, two teenage girls and one adult woman, were rescued. One of the teenagers was transported to a hospital where she was treated and released while the others did not require hospital treatment. The fourth swimmer, a 41 year old man, could not be recovered. Rescue efforts continued into the next day but officials called off the search that afternoon when they were still unable to locate the man. His body was found 5 days later on July 5th by a fishing charter roughly two miles offshore from Dempster Street Beach. Severe drought conditions developed across much of northern and northeastern Illinois during the middle and latter parts of October. Precipitation over the area was far below normal for the month. The Rockford Airport recorded just 0.79 of rain for the entire month, 2.63 below their October normal. Chicago-O'Hare fell 2.25 short of normal having recorded 1.18, while the NWS Chicago office in Romeoville recorded 0.95 during October falling 2.72 shy of normal. Numerous wildfires occurred in October around NWS Chicago's county warning area, including one near Herscher in Kankakee County that destroyed over 300 acres worth of crops. The severe drought continued into November.

Severe drought conditions carried into November from an abnormally dry October. However, frequent bouts of rain improved drought conditions throughout the first few weeks of November. O'Hare Airport ended the month with 3.63 of rain, 1.2 more than its monthly average of 2.42. The Rockford Airport fell only about 0.2 shy of its monthly normal with 2.04.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An area of thunderstorms moved across east central Illinois during the afternoon of May 16th producing damaging convective wind gusts across southern Ford and southern Iroquois Counties.  These high winds created a dust storm that raced north across northeast Illinois during the late afternoon and early evening of May 16th.  Visibilities were near zero in many areas with wind gusts of up to 55 to 65 mph.  The worst conditions lasted 15 to 30 minutes at any one location and then gradually improved.  A large tree was blown down onto a house in Piper City causing significant structural damage.  A few thunderstorms also developed across far northern Illinois producing isolated large hail.
